objective: Qualify test-only MPFR thread-cache cleanup and a nonleaking dispatch-label fixture on a new copy of the unchanged normal-image runtime prototype.
review: The private helper is compiled only in unit/integration tests. Rug remains a dev-dependency; no manifest, production arithmetic, representation, geometry, policy or cache budget changes.

31 oracle entry points register a thread-local destructor before MPFR use. Multiple registrations reuse the same thread-local guard; the cache remains available throughout the test, then FreeCache::Local runs at thread exit.
The local destructor avoids shared/global cache teardown while other test workers may be active. Local Float values drop before thread teardown, including on unwinding.

Two shared-oracle helper functions (assert_enclosed and mpfr_text) inherit registration from every calling test. Rational/Integer-only Rug tests do not use MPFR caches. No Rug-using test entry point launches a worker which uses Rug without registration.

The tracing fixture replaces six leaked four-byte string allocations with six distinct four-byte slots in one immutable static array. The existing unequal-pointer assertion and merged-count assertion remain.
Every pre-existing file changed by this patch is byte-identical in the parent runtime prototype and admitted root before this patch, permitting later separate review of test-only admission.
validation: Strict release all-target Hyperreal Clippy, default and all features.
Format both control sources; build and run a deliberate heap-overflow control, requiring exit 66 and the actual ASan diagnostic.
Build a Rug-only control importing the actual candidate helper, using the frozen prior ASan Rug/native libraries.

Run two-worker controls for ordinary exit and one deliberate unwinding exit. Require leak detection enabled, both process exits zero, empty stderr, repeated helper registration, and unchanged numeric witnesses.
Run every Hyperreal/Hyperlimit/Hypermesh library and integration test, default and all features, with two test threads and leak detection enabled.
Run the original native hull determinism regression with one test thread and leak detection enabled.
execution_context: Native LeakSanitizer execution requires exec_command require_escalated because the frozen standalone environment control established sandbox thread-attachment denial. No suppressions or disabled leak detection.
limits: This is a new finite test-harness qualification. Earlier ASan failures remain closed and preserved; this run does not complete or replace either failed run.
The Rust standard library is not rebuilt with ASan. Host procedural macros and GMP/MPFR C code are not claimed instrumented; their intercepted heap allocations are checked by LeakSanitizer.
The cleanup inventory covers the selected unit/integration tests, not standalone comparison programs or every benchmark in the repository.
This is not a performance trial, exhaustive fuzzing, a formal proof, full CI validation, push readiness, or admission of the scalar/mesh runtime prototypes.
